title: Slide 1 · Quantifiers and rules
question: Ava and Lin both requested C1. If you leave the person’s name blank in Requested(person, C1), how many matching names should you find in those records?
answer: Two. Keeping C1 fixed makes each of the two requesters a match.

title: Slide 2 · Say who a statement covers
question: Which single record is enough to disprove “every listed borrower completed orientation”?
answer: Bo’s explicit no is a counterexample. Ava’s yes establishes the claim for Ava only.

title: Slide 3 · Find a witness
question: If Bo also completes orientation, is Ava still a witness? How many witnesses are there?
answer: Yes. The claim allows any positive number of witnesses. With both records set to yes, Ava and Bo each provide one.

title: Slide 4 · Apply an if–then policy
question: Someone tells you Bo is eligible. Does the arrow also establish that Bo completed orientation?
answer: No. This rule gives a sufficient route to eligibility. Another policy might grant eligibility by a different route. Reasoning backwards from Eligible(Bo) would require more information.

title: Slide 5 · Keep names aligned across conditions
question: C2 is also available. Can the rule mark Ava’s C2 request ready using just these records?
answer: No. The request list ties Ava to C1. Available(C2) cannot supply the missing Requested(Ava, C2).

title: Slide 6 · Follow the person and camera through the rule
question: Replace this line: eligible = {"Ava"} with: eligible = {"Bo"} What will print?
answer:
Bo C1
Both people requested C1, but the revised eligible set contains only Bo. Camera C1 still passes the availability check.

title: Slide 8 · From this module to the next
question: A rule covers every piece of equipment. The list calls T2 a tripod. What general statement about tripods would let you apply the rule to T2?
answer: If every tripod is equipment, T2’s recorded type puts it in the group covered by the rule. You can use the same statement for a newly listed tripod.

title: Office hours · If a borrower is missing from the orientation log, does that disprove the claim that everyone completed orientation?
question: If a borrower is missing from the orientation log, does that disprove the claim that everyone completed orientation?
answer: It depends on what the log records. A complete checked roster with an explicit no supplies a counterexample. A missing entry in a partial log gives an unknown. First identify the set of people in the claim, then check what counts as evidence about each person.

title: Office hours · Why keep both Requested and Ready in the model?
question: Why keep both Requested and Ready in the model?
answer: Ava can ask for C1 even while it is unavailable. Requested captures her action. Ready captures a conclusion that also depends on eligibility and availability. Keeping both lets the desk explain which condition a pending request still needs.

title: Exercise 1
question: A complete list marks Ava yes, Bo yes, and Lin no for orientation. Give a witness and a counterexample for the relevant quantified claims.
answer: Ava (or Bo) witnesses the first claim. Lin’s explicit no disproves the second.

title: Exercise 2
question: Requested(Ava, C2), Eligible(Ava), and Available(C1) are recorded. Trace each variable in the ready rule.
answer: The request fixes p = Ava and i = C2. Eligibility matches Ava. Availability is known for C1 only, so this rule cannot conclude Ready(Ava, C2).

title: Exercise 3
question: Compare “every borrower requested some camera” with “some camera was requested by every borrower.” Give a two-request example that separates them.
answer: If Ava requested only C1 and Bo requested only C2, each borrower has a camera they requested. There is no single camera both requested. The order of the two quantifiers changes what must be shared.

title: Lab case 1 · Counterexample
question: Does the evidence establish orientation for everyone on the roster, for at least one person, or for both?
answer: The existential claim holds with Ava as its witness. Bo’s explicit no is a counterexample to the universal claim.

title: Lab case 2 · Names do not match
question: Does any request qualify as ready for review?
answer: The only request fixes p as Ava. Eligible(Bo) cannot establish Eligible(Ava), so the rule yields no ready request from these records.

title: Lab case 3 · Two eligible requests
question: Does the ready rule select one winner?
answer: It derives Ready(Ava, C1) and Ready(Bo, C1). Both requests meet the conditions for review. The rule contains no tie-breaker and makes no allocation.
